findings.failure_path: On Codex and Claude, SessionStart rewrites the link to $PLUGIN_ROOT/agent-context/session-policy.md, and the new proposed-next-stop.sh needs $PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/host-input.py. Only the OpenCode closure is asserted. The Makefile/release file list that builds the native marketplace plugin is not in this packet. If either file is left out, startup points at a policy file that does not exist, and the Stop hook just prints 'normalizer missing', so the shared isolation guard's dependency degrades. No native-package test here would catch that.
findings.smallest_fix: Add a package test that asserts marketplace/plugins/ccl-skills/{hooks/host-input.py,agent-context/session-policy.md} are in release.files and the packed tarball, and that the rendered policy path exists.

findings.failure_path: The 9600-byte check only swaps out the recovery capsule. If the bootstrap plus the rendered absolute policy path goes over budget by itself (a long PLUGIN_ROOT, or the compact entry growing), the output still exceeds the direct-context budget. Codex then spills it, and the claim that essential rules stay directly visible fails silently. No test pins the bootstrap size.
findings.smallest_fix: Recompute bytes after the replacement. Emit a stderr diagnostic when it is still over budget, and add a test that caps the rendered bootstrap size.

findings.failure_path: A same-version install returns {...doctor(context), message:'hooks trust remains pending/unverified'}. Doctor can now return code 0 with status installed-hooks-trusted, so the result combines a trusted status with a pending-trust message. Consumers reading the message get the wrong trust state.
findings.smallest_fix: Only override the message when doctor's status is installed-hooks-pending, or reuse doctor's message.

concern_results.conclusion: parseHookInventory accepts every package hook only when its handler matches, its source is the verified snapshot or a hash-verified cache root in the right namespace, and there are no diagnostics. Worker cleanup kills the whole process group. The weak spots: this packet cannot show that the Codex/Claude plugin build ships host-input.py and session-policy.md, because the Makefile diff is missing. The startup byte budget also has no check when the bootstrap itself is too large. And a same-version install gives a contradictory trust message.

No trust approval or hook execution was found in doctor. Trust results always carry runtime=unverified. Foreign, similarly named and wrong-namespace plugins cannot certify health, and the tests exercise those cases. For native plugin packages, installed-asset closure has no evidence in this packet, so that containment claim is still unverified.
